paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Everybody around that cross had a dare ready. "Come down from the cross and save Yourself!" (Mark 15:30). The chief priests and scribes said, "He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!" (Mark 15:31). Read that line one more time, because it's the kind of thing that sounds like an insult and lands like a headline.

The people mocking Him thought staying on that cross meant He was powerless. I think staying was the whole point. Mark's Gospel says elsewhere that the Son of Man came "to give His life as a ransom for many" (Mark 10:45). So when He doesn't come down, He isn't losing. He's doing exactly what He came to do, for you and for me.

And look who finally gets it. It isn't the crowd or the leaders. It's a Roman centurion standing right in front of Him, who says, "Truly this man was the Son of God!" (Mark 15:39). The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom (Mark 15:38), and I think that's a loud sign something big just happened. So here's the takeaway, baker: when God's way looks like weakness, don't walk away. Stay and watch, because the cross is where it shows. And friend, this story isn't over.
